targetText: III Part I The Conversion of Surplus-Value into Profit and of the Rate of Surplus-Value into the Rate of Profit Chapter 6.
explanation: The rate of profit ($p/C$) measures surplus value relative to total invested capital (constant plus variable), whereas the rate of surplus value ($s/v$) measures exploitation relative to labor costs alone.

targetText: Owing to this falling tendency, the other portion of the value representing raw material increases proportionally, unless this increase is counterbalanced by a proportionate decrease in the value of the raw material arising from the growing productivity of the labour employed in its own production.
explanation: The tendential fall of the rate of profit occurs because technological progress increases constant capital faster than living labor power, shrinking the relative source of surplus value.
